question: The line joining the points $A(2,-1,3)$ and $B(k,5,-3)$ has direction ratios proportional to $2,3,-3$. Determine the value of $k$, and hence obtain the direction cosines, vector equation and Cartesian equation of the directed line from $A$ to $B$.
explanation:
Required Condition
The direction ratios of the line joining $A(2,-1,3)$ to $B(k,5,-3)$ are
$$k-2,\;5-(-1),\;-3-3$$
that is,
$$k-2,\;6,\;-6$$

These are proportional to $2,3,-3$. Hence,
$$\frac{k-2}{2}=\frac{6}{3}=\frac{-6}{-3}$$
Since $\frac{6}{3}=2$, we get
$$\frac{k-2}{2}=2$$
Therefore, $k-2=4$, giving
$$k=6$$
Thus, $B=(6,5,-3)$.

The direction ratios of $AB$ are $4,6,-6$, which are proportional to the simpler set $2,3,-3$. Their magnitude factor is
$$\sqrt{2^2+3^2+(-3)^2}=\sqrt{22}$$
Therefore, the direction cosines of the directed line from $A$ to $B$ are
$$\frac{2}{\sqrt{22}},\;\frac{3}{\sqrt{22}},\;-\frac{3}{\sqrt{22}}$$

Formation of Equation
The position vector of $A$ is $2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$, and a vector parallel to the line is $2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-3\hat{k}$. Hence, the vector equation is
$$\vec{r}=(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\hat{k})+\lambda(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-3\hat{k})$$
Thus,
$$x=2+2\lambda,\quad y=-1+3\lambda,\quad z=3-3\lambda$$
Eliminating $\lambda$, we obtain
$$\frac{x-2}{2}=\frac{y+1}{3}=\frac{z-3}{-3}$$

Final Result
The required value is $k=6$. The direction cosines are $\frac{2}{\sqrt{22}},\frac{3}{\sqrt{22}},-\frac{3}{\sqrt{22}}$, the vector equation is $\vec{r}=(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\hat{k})+\lambda(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-3\hat{k})$, and the Cartesian equation is $\frac{x-2}{2}=\frac{y+1}{3}=\frac{z-3}{-3}$.

options.B: $k=6$; direction cosines $\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{22}},-\frac{3}{\sqrt{22}},\frac{3}{\sqrt{22}}\right)$; $\vec r=(2\hat i-\hat j+3\hat k)+\lambda(2\hat i-3\hat j+3\hat k)$
